title: Needle-lattice latency-cost annotated gloss
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working sketch of a compact collateral piece that shows a small-number-of-strategies comparison across latency percentiles and cost-per-1k-tokens. The goal is a visual/text brief that product/solutions can drop into decks: highlight where small changes to batching/prefetch/tiling produce disproportionate $/1k wins or p99 penalties.

Test scope and constraints:
- Workload: conversational assistant traces sampled from production (10k sessions, mixed short/long) but replayed in a controlled harness.
- Model: 13B open variant (quantized 4-bit) served on gpus we use in Dedicated.
- Network: intra-region, no cross-region failover during tests.
- Key metric pairs: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) and effective $/1k tokens (hosted equivalent).
- Measurement period: sustained 30-minute windows at three load-points (sparse: 200 qps, mid: 1k qps, surge: 4k qps). This doc focuses on the mid-load window.

Strategies compared (names are shorthand used in the harness):
- on-demand: single-request fastpath, minimal batching, immediate scheduling (baseline).
- intent-prefetch: recent-turn prefix prefetch + KV warm cache before decode.
- microbatch-8: opportunistic batching up to 8 tokens/requests; preserves latency SLOs for short responses by admitting small batches.
- multiplex-16: client multiplexing with larger multiplex windows (higher packing efficiency).
- tiling-tilt: slotized tiling strategy that packs multiple sessions for longer-decode efficiency (trade: slightly higher p50).

Key table (mid-load window):

Strategy | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $ / 1k tokens
-----------------------------------------------------
on-demand   | 48     | 220    | 860    | $0.89
intent-pref | 54     | 140    | 380    | $0.64
microbatch-8| 62     | 160    | 420    | $0.47
multiplex-16| 58     | 145    | 390    | $0.35
tiling-tilt | 72     | 180    | 510    | $0.40

Observations from the numbers above:
- Big cost swing: on-demand vs multiplex-16 shows ~60% drop in $/1k at roughly similar p50/p95 (on-demand p95 is dominated by underutilized kernels).
- p99 sensitivity: the highest cost-savings strategies (multiplex, microbatch) still have material p99 improvements over intent-prefetch, but tiling-tilt regresses p50 in exchange for sustained-dollar wins for long sessions.
- intent-prefetch reduces p95 significantly compared to on-demand while also saving cost, making it a good candidate for the 'fast but cheaper' lane.

Text kiteplot (compact ascii "lattice" view):
Each line shows relative position (scale: 0..10) where 10 is best for latency (lower ms) and best for cost (lower $ -> higher score). This is not precise numeric plotting — it's a quick glance tradeoff lattice for PMs.

Latency (lower is better) scale: we invert to show higher-is-better for the kiteplot. Cost (lower is better) inverted similarly.

Name         | Latency-score (10 best) | Cost-score (10 best)
-----------------------------------------------------------
on-demand     | #######... (6)           | ###........ (3)
intent-pref   | ########.. (8)           | #####..... (5)
microbatch-8  | #######... (7)           | #######... (7)
multiplex-16  | ########.. (8)           | #########. (9)
tiling-tilt   | #####...... (5)           | #######... (7)

(Interpretation: multiplex-16 sits near the top-right in this compact lattice — good latency and much better cost; tiling helps cost for long tails but loses p50.)

Session-sliced mini heatmap (p99 delta vs baseline):
- Short sessions (< 40 tokens): multiplex-16 p99 -20% vs baseline; microbatch no significant win; intent-prefetch +/- 0
- Medium (40-320 tokens): microbatch-8 p99 -45%; multiplex-16 p99 -55%
- Long (>320 tokens): tiling-tilt p99 -30% and $/1k -25% (tiling amortizes decode work)

Representative ASCII sparkline of cost per minute under mid load (lower is better):
(on-demand)    $----****------$ (peak wastage)
(intent-pref)  $---***---**---$
(microbatch-8) $--**--**--**-$
(multiplex-16) $-*--*--*--*--$
(tiling-tilt)  $--**--*---**--$

Notes on methodology caveats (things to call out when this goes into collateral):
- These numbers are for a single model/config on Dedicated hardware; hosted pricing equivalents assume identical utilization which is optimistic for small tenants.
- We did not exercise region fallbacks or multi-tenant interference patterns; real-world p99 may shift right.
- Network jitter smoothing and client-side chunking can change p50 by ~5-10ms independently of server strategy.
- Cost model here includes GPU amortized token cost + steady-state infra. It excludes long-tail storage/eval infra.

Qualitative recommendations (for product/cs handoff):
1) For PLG-hosted: default to multiplex-16 for non-interactive flows (chat summaries, embeddings in bulk). It gives big $ wins with little latency downside.
2) For interactive assistant tier (SLA-sensitive): enable intent-prefetch by default (small CPU/KV warm overhead, large p95 win).
3) For high-throughput enterprise Dedicated: expose tiling-tilt as a deploy knob for long-session-heavy customers (saves $/1k for transcripts / long chats).
4) Expose a policy in Console: per-route recommended strategy with a quick-sim button showing expected p99 vs $/1k based on recent traffic mix.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (short list):
- Validate multiplex behavior with multi-tenant interference (JIRA:OBS-4321) — schedule a mixed-tenant run.
- Run same harness with a 70B quantized variant to see whether tiling benefits amplify (TODO: Evan to spin infra ticket).
- Add small section showing latency-cost effect under cold-start-dominated windows (we currently only show sustained mid-load).

Short-term action items (next 2 weeks):
- Create a polished PNG of the kiteplot + the 1-table summary for GTM slide deck (owner: Maya)
- Schedule cross-team sync with Pricing to align hosted-equivalent $/1k assumptions (owner: Luis)
- Add multiplex telemetry hooks (slot fill rate, packing ratio) to Console to enable route-level recommendations (owner: Aisha)

Appendix: quick-run harness flags used (informal)
- replay-sample=prod-10k-may2028
- model=13B-quant-v2
- slotization=tiling-tilt|microbatch-8|multiplex-16|intent-prefetch|on-demand
- load=mid-1k

Rough internal references: confluence:OBS-needle-lattice-2028 for calibration notes; JIRA:OBS-4321 for follow-up mixed-tenant runs.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally short — the goal is an explanatory slide + one-pager. We may expand to include cold-window and surge-window slices if stakeholders push.

---
summary: Working draft comparing 5 serving strategies (on-demand, intent-prefetch, microbatch-8, multiplex-16, tiling-tilt) for mid-load conversational traces. Includes ASCII lattice/kiteplot, tables for p50/p95/p99 and $/1k tokens, recommendations and action items.
